transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… mostly work, I guess. They got scared because I kept sort of freezing up in the middle of service. Like, I’d be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was supposed to be closing checks, but instead I was just repeating table numbers.

And it sounds stupid when I say it like that, but it kept happening—like doing things out of order. The soda station is right by where we keep the lemons, and I remember thinking the lemons looked… anyway, people were staring, and my manager said I needed to come talk to someone.
When you looked at the lemons, did they seem different from how they really are?

I don’t know if they were different, exactly. I mean, they were just lemons, I think. Sometimes when I’m at that station I get caught on little things, like how the light hits the peel, or the stickers on them—our produce guy puts them in the same bin every time, and once he brought these really tiny limes by mistake and everyone made jokes about it all night.

But… no, I’m not sure they changed or anything. I just remember staring too long.
When you freeze up like that, do you suddenly feel very intense fear or panic?

I don’t know if I’d call it panic. I mean, I get embarrassed after, because everyone’s looking and then I can’t remember if table 12 wanted no ice or if that was table 14, and the tickets start stacking up.

Fear… maybe not suddenly. It’s more like my head sort of catches on something and then everything else keeps moving without me. Panic sounds like when people can’t breathe or their chest hurts—my cousin used to say that happened to her in college, before she switched majors. I don’t think it’s exactly like that for me.
During those moments when you freeze, do you feel detached from yourself or like the situation around you isn’t quite real?

I’m… not sure. I don’t think I’m floating outside myself or anything like that. It’s more like I lose the thread, like when you walk into the walk-in cooler and forget why you’re there, except everyone can see it happening.

The room is still the room, I think. The soda station is still sticky and the ice machine is still making that grinding noise—our ice machine has been weird for months, actually, and the repair guy always comes during lunch rush, which is ridiculous. But… yeah, I don’t know about “not real.” I haven’t really noticed it that way.
When this happens, do you feel confused?

Yeah… confused, I guess. Not like I don’t know where I am, but I stop doing the thing I’m supposed to be doing. Like at work I’ll be in the middle of service and suddenly I’m just standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, saying table numbers over and over instead of closing out checks.

That’s what scared people, I think. Because it’s dinner rush and everyone needs something, and I’m doing it all wrong or not in the right order. Then someone has to tell me, like, “You were supposed to cash out table 9,” and I’m still thinking about table 12 or 14 or whichever one.
Have you had any recent head injury, seizure, fever, or new drug or medication use?

I don’t think so… I mean, I haven’t, like, hit my head or anything that I remember. No one’s said I had a seizure. Fever, I don’t know—I don’t really check unless I feel really awful, and I’ve been going to work because if you call out they act like the whole restaurant is going to collapse, even though people call out all the time.

New drugs or medicine… no, not that I can think of. I’m trying to remember because sometimes the cold medicine aisle all looks the same, and once I bought the non-drowsy one but it still made me feel weird, but recently? I don’t think there’s anything new.
After one of these episodes, are there parts of what happened that you can’t remember?

I don’t really know. I mean, people tell me afterward what I was doing, and sometimes it feels… blurry, like I wasn’t keeping track of the order of things. But I can remember pieces, like where I was standing or what I had in my hand.

It’s not like waking up from sleep or anything. More like when someone tells you a story and you realize you missed the middle because you were watching the coffee machine drip too slow—ours at work does that and everyone complains but no one cleans it right. So… I guess I’m not sure if I can’t remember, or if I just wasn’t paying attention right then.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people could not?

Yeah… I mean, sometimes. Not like seeing a person standing there or anything, at least I don’t think so.

But I’ll hear a woman’s voice say my name. Like during closing, when we’re counting out or doing the receipts, or when I’m at home in the kitchen, and it’ll be clear enough that I answer back before I realize nobody else reacted. Sometimes it says I’m doing the count wrong, which—people say that at work anyway, because everyone has their own way of closing and the register tape never tears right, it curls up and gets lost under the little coin tray.

But the weird part is nobody else hears it. Like I’ll look over and they’re just doing whatever they were doing, and then I feel stupid because I already said, “What?” out loud.
When you hear the woman’s voice say your name, does it sound like it’s coming from outside you, as if someone in the room is speaking?

Yeah… I mean, it sounds like it’s in the room, I guess. Like somebody just off to the side said my name, clear enough that I’ll answer, “What?” before I even think about it.

It happens sometimes when I’m closing at work, or at home in the kitchen. The work ones bother me more because we’re counting and everyone’s already tense about the drawer being off by like two dollars, and then I hear this woman saying I’m doing the count wrong. But then I look around and nobody’s reacting, like no one heard anything, so… I don’t know. It feels outside of me when it happens.
Before these problems started, were you sick with anything like an infection or another medical illness?

I don’t think so… not that I remember. I mean, I get colds like anybody, especially working around people and all their half-finished cups and napkins, and there was that one winter everyone at work had some cough that kept going around because nobody stays home when rent’s due.

But before all this started? I don’t remember being really sick, like with some big infection or anything. I’m not sure what would count, though.
Did these problems start soon after something very upsetting or stressful happened to you?

I don’t know if it was one big upsetting thing, exactly. It kind of started after they asked me to take on the evening shift lead stuff at work… like closing, making sure things were counted right, people asking me where everything goes.

And I thought it was fine at first, because it’s just work, you know? People make such a big deal about who gets which section and who rolled silverware wrong, and then the schedule gets changed three times. But looking back, this whole change in me has been building since then… about a year and two months now, I think.
Do you believe someone is trying to harm you or control you?

I don’t know if “harm” is the word… not like somebody’s waiting outside for me. But I do feel like a couple of the servers are watching how I ring things in, like they’re waiting for me to mess up.

And there’s this one regular customer too, he always orders almost the same thing but changes one little part, and then the ticket comes back weird or there’ll be a mark on it, or something circled, and it feels like… like they’re leaving signs to show I did it wrong so they can get me fired.

My husband says restaurants are just messy and tickets get mixed up all the time, and maybe that’s true, but it doesn’t feel random when it keeps happening.
Have you found yourself caring much less about seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess so. I used to like doing little things, like walking on the beach when it wasn’t too crowded, or baking something on my day off, or messing with the garden. I had a journal too, but now it just sits there.

My husband will try to talk to me, like tell me about something from his day, and I’m listening but also not really… I just sit there. It’s like I can’t get myself to start anything, or care enough to keep doing it. Even simple stuff feels like it takes this big push.
During these episodes, do you ever not know where you are?

I don’t think so… I mean, I know where I am, like if I’m at work or at home. Sometimes I’ll kind of lose track of what I was doing, like I’ll go into the kitchen and then forget why, but everybody does that, right?

It’s more like I get stuck thinking about something and then the room feels… busy, or I’m not paying attention. Like at the restaurant, people are calling for ranch and extra napkins and the printer is spitting tickets, and then suddenly I realize I’ve been standing there too long. But I don’t think I’ve ever actually not known where I was.
At any point during these problems, have you felt drowsy or hard to stay awake?

Drowsy… not really, I don’t think. I mean, sometimes I’m tired after a shift, but that’s just being on my feet and people asking for refills all night, you know?

Hard to stay awake… no, I don’t think I’m nodding off or anything. It’s more like my mind gets stuck somewhere else, but I’m awake. At least I think I am.
Have you felt that some outside force is controlling your thoughts or actions?

I don’t know if I’d say controlling exactly… like not moving my arms or anything. But at work, it feels like people are kind of… pushing things in a direction.

There are a couple servers, and this one regular customer, and I keep feeling like they’re watching how I ring things in. Like if I comp something wrong or forget to add a side, then there’ll be these little signs on the tickets, like they’re leaving them there to prove I’m messing up so I’ll get fired.

My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mistakes, because tickets get messy all the time, especially when it’s busy, but… it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like they’re trying to make me do something wrong, or catch me doing it.
Did these problems come on suddenly, or did they build up gradually?

It was more gradual, I think. Not like one day I woke up different. It’s been… maybe a year and a couple months? Like since they asked me to start doing the evening shift lead stuff.

At first I thought it was just the extra responsibility, because evenings are a mess sometimes—people don’t tip right, the kitchen gets backed up, everyone wants to blame the server—but then it just sort of kept building. So, yeah, not sudden. More like it crept up.

My husband will try to talk to me, like tell me about something from his day, and I’m listening but also not really… I just sit there. It’s like I can’t get myself to start anything, or care enough to keep doing it. Even simple stuff feels like it takes this big push.

No clear medical trigger, but F06.0 remains as a rule-out pending medical workup.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are occurring in the context of fluctuating consciousness or disorientation, which would point toward an organic delirium-like process (F06.0) rather than schizophrenia (F20.0) or acute psychosis (F23.9).
doctor.question: During these episodes, do you ever not know where you are?

target_item.reason: The question asks about disorientation or not knowing where I am during episodes, which is not specifically covered by the symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… I mean, I know where I am, like if I’m at work or at home. Sometimes I’ll kind of lose track of what I was doing, like I’ll go into the kitchen and then forget why, but everybody does that, right?

It’s more like I get stuck thinking about something and then the room feels… busy, or I’m not paying attention. Like at the restaurant, people are calling for ranch and extra napkins and the printer is spitting tickets, and then suddenly I realize I’ve been standing there too long. But I don’t think I’ve ever actually not known where I was.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a clear disturbance in consciousness/attention suggestive of delirium from a medical cause rather than a primary psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: At any point during these problems, have you felt drowsy or hard to stay awake?

target_item.reason: The question is about drowsiness or difficulty staying awake, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Drowsy… not really, I don’t think. I mean, sometimes I’m tired after a shift, but that’s just being on my feet and people asking for refills all night, you know?

Hard to stay awake… no, I don’t think I’m nodding off or anything. It’s more like my mind gets stuck somewhere else, but I’m awake. At least I think I am.

doctor.intent: Determine whether she has persistent delusions of external control, which would favor schizophrenia over brief psychosis or a medical delirium state.
doctor.question: Have you felt that some outside force is controlling your thoughts or actions?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I keep feeling like a couple of the servers and one of the regular customers are watching how I ring things in and leaving little signs on the tickets to prove they're trying to get me fired, even when my husband says it’s just normal restaurant mess-ups.
target_item.reason: The question asks about a belief that an outside force is controlling thoughts or actions, which is a type of delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d say controlling exactly… like not moving my arms or anything. But at work, it feels like people are kind of… pushing things in a direction.

There are a couple servers, and this one regular customer, and I keep feeling like they’re watching how I ring things in. Like if I comp something wrong or forget to add a side, then there’ll be these little signs on the tickets, like they’re leaving them there to prove I’m messing up so I’ll get fired.

My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mistakes, because tickets get messy all the time, especially when it’s busy, but… it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like they’re trying to make me do something wrong, or catch me doing it.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there has been a marked, abrupt change from baseline suggesting an acute psychotic or organic process versus a more gradual schizophrenia-spectrum course.
doctor.question: Did these problems come on suddenly, or did they build up gradually?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This whole change in me has been building for about a year and two months, since I was asked to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the onset and course of the problems, which is covered by the duration profile describing that the changes built up over about a year and two months.

patient.answer:
It was more gradual, I think. Not like one day I woke up different. It’s been… maybe a year and a couple months? Like since they asked me to start doing the evening shift lead stuff.

At first I thought it was just the extra responsibility, because evenings are a mess sometimes—people don’t tip right, the kitchen gets backed up, everyone wants to blame the server—but then it just sort of kept building. So, yeah, not sudden. More like it crept up.

inference.note: Gradual onset over >1 year with persistent auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusional ideas, disorganization/freezing, and negative symptoms strongly supports schizophrenia; this rules against F23.9 (not acute/transient) and makes F06.0 less likely given no evidence of delirium/medical cause, no clouding of consciousness, and preserved orientation.

opening_question.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a gradual onset over about 14 months of persistent psychotic symptoms including clear third-person/external auditory hallucinations and persecutory/paranoid delusional beliefs, along with negative symptoms such as reduced interest, diminished motivation, and social withdrawal. Functional impairment is evident at work, with disorganized behavior/confusion during service. There is no evidence from the interview that symptoms are better explained by panic, dissociation, delirium, substance use, head injury, or another acute medical cause. This presentation is most consistent with schizophrenia, paranoid type in ICD-10.
